headline: Day-Use Passes Required for Alpine Access
reservation: Access to Joffre Lakes requires a Day-Use Pass during peak seasonal windows, which is distinct from camping permits. These passes are released in short-term rolling windows and are often fully claimed minutes after release; always verify the current BC Parks reservation schedule before departing Vancouver or Pemberton.

days.title: Glacial Basin Ascent

stops.name: Lower Joffre Lake
stops.detail: Reach the first turquoise basin within minutes of the trailhead to observe the Matier Glacier reflection before the wind rises.

stops.name: Middle Joffre Lake
stops.detail: Ascend the main switchbacks to reach the largest of the three lakes, known for its vibrant silt-driven color and floating log features.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes from Pemberton; conditions vary with mountain weather.
days.note: The trail involves significant elevation gain on uneven terrain; pace yourself for the thinner mountain air.

days.title: Upper Alpine and Icefall Views

stops.name: Upper Joffre Lake
stops.detail: Trek to the base of the Matier Glacier moraine where the water is coldest and the granite peaks are most prominent.

stops.name: Holloway Falls
stops.detail: Pause at the cascading waters between the middle and upper lakes, a popular spot for observing the local sub-alpine flora.

days.driving: Minimal driving if staged at the park; allow for shuttle transit if active.
days.note: Stay on marked paths to protect the sensitive alpine heather and meadows.

days.title: Pemberton Valley Transit

stops.name: Nairn Falls Provincial Park
stops.detail: Observe the 60-meter high waterfall where the Green River carves through the rock on your return toward Whistler.

stops.name: One Mile Lake
stops.detail: Enjoy a flat boardwalk stroll through the wetlands near Pemberton to decompress after the steep Joffre terrain.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the transit between the park and Pemberton valley sights.
days.note: Expect high traffic volumes on Highway 99 during summer weekends.

intel.title: Restricted Trail Entry
intel.text: Capacity is strictly managed via the BC Parks pass system; those without a digital pass will be turned away by staff at the Highway 99 entry. Check for seasonal closures related to First Nations cultural celebrations or conservation.

intel.title: Overflow Limitations
intel.text: The primary lot at the trailhead fills rapidly, and parking on the shoulder of Highway 99 is strictly prohibited and subject to towing. Use official shuttle services from Duffey Lake Road if they are operational during your visit.

intel.title: Zero Connectivity
intel.text: There is no cellular service along this stretch of the Duffey Lake Road or on the trails. Download all offline maps and your digital pass QR code before leaving Pemberton.

intel.title: Pemberton Supply Gap
intel.text: Pemberton is the final reliable stop for fuel and food before heading north into the mountain pass. Ensure your tank is full as there are no services between the park and Lillooet.

intel.title: Seasonal Snowpack
intel.text: Snow can persist on the Upper Lake trail well into July, requiring appropriate footwear. Early autumn visits should account for shorter daylight hours in the deep valley shadows.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at YVR, secure bear spray and water supplies in Squamish or Whistler, and check into Pemberton lodging.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are sufficient for Highway 99, but ensure rental contracts allow for mountain pass driving.
plan.goldenHour: Upper Joffre Lake viewpoint for alpenglow on Matier Glacier; timing varies significantly by month.
